label: Diffuse_Large_B_Cell_Lymphoma_NOS
query: Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma NOS
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS) is a common B-cell neoplasm with extranodal involvements like CNS and bone marrow.
- Characterized by a high Ki-67 proliferation index, usually below 95%.
- Associated with longstanding pyothorax, pulmonary tuberculosis history, EBV infection, and cytokines.
- Essential immunophenotype includes CD20 positivity.
- Prognosis is aggressive; 5-year survival rate is 20-35%.

## Terminology
- Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOT otherwise specified (DLBCL-NOS).
- ICD-O code 9680/3: Malignant lymphoma, large B cell, diffuse, NOS.

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Diffuse proliferation of medium or large lymphoid cells with centroblastic or immunoblastic morphology.
  - Mature B-cell immunophenotype, generally CD20 positive.
- **Desirable:**
  - High Ki-67 index but less than 95%.
  - Absence of MYC rearrangements.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Associated with longstanding pyothorax and a history of pulmonary tuberculosis or tuberculous pleuritis.
- EBV infection and cytokines like IL-10 and IL-6 contribute to pathogenesis.
- Involvement of reactive oxygen species in pyothorax ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/lymphomadiffusepyo.html)).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Common form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
- **Presentation:**
  - Symptoms include chest pain, fever, swelling, and respiratory symptoms.
- **Prognosis:**
  - Aggressive behavior with a 5-year survival rate of 20-35%.
  - Better outcomes for patients achieving complete remission with therapy.

## Microscopic
- Diffuse growth pattern with effacement of architecture.
- Cells often exhibit centroblastic or immunoblastic features.
- Prominent necrosis and angiocentric growth can occur.

![Centroblastic cytology](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/PEDS/18960.jpg)
![Ileum with smaller blasts](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/PEDS/18961.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - CD20 positive.
  - CD79a positive.
  - Negative for TdT, CD10, BCL6, and HHV8.
- **Molecular Genetics:**
  - Generally lacks MYC rearrangements.

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Primary Effusion Lymphoma:**
  - Often KSHV/HHV8 positive, immunodeficient history.
- **KSHV/HHV8-positive DLBCL:**
  - Associated with KSHV/HHV8; positive immunostaining for LANA.
- **Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma NOS:**
  - Heterogeneous T-cell features; lacks CD20 positivity.
- **Thymic B-cell Lymphomas:**
  - Includes PMBCL and classic Hodgkin lymphoma ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_HEME/Thymic_B_Cell_Lymphomas.html)).
- **Splenic B-cell Lymphoma:**
  - Includes primary splenic large B-cell lymphoma ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_HEME/Splenic_B_Cell_Lymphoma.html)).

![CNS with blastoid cytology](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/PEDS/18962.jpg)

This section focuses on PMBCL and its differential diagnosis with these lymphomas, as the other diseases and systemic lymphomas involving the thymus, the commonest of which is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS), are discussed elsewhere in this volume. PMBCL is a mature aggressive B-cell lymphoma of putative thymic B-cell origin, arising in the anterior mediastinum. It represents 2–3% of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Familial clustering of PMBCL cases has been reported based on shared genetic mutations. PMBCL occurs predominantly in young adults in their third decade, with a female predominance of 2:1, but it can also occur in children. Patients commonly present with cough, dyspnoea, and/or dysphagia, and many patients have bulky anterior mediastinal masses that can be associated with the superior vena cava syndrome. cards.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS Section: microscopic PTCL-NOS can cause complete or partial effacement of the lymph node architecture. In most cases the pattern is diffuse, with medium to large pleomorphic cells. Less common cases with pleomorphic small and large cells are also described [[WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Haematolymphoid tumours. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2024. (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11). https://publications.iarc.who.int/637.]]. Small lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells, and histiocytes are present in the background. Haemophagocytosis can occasionally be detected. Residual atrophic follicles can be present. Clustered and scattered epithelioid histiocytes are frequently seen. cards.title: KSHV/HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: KSHV/HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma definition: Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus / human herpesvirus 8 (KSHV/HHV8)-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a large B-cell lymphoma consistently associated with KSHV/HHV8, in general arising in patients with profound immunodeficiency, but it may occur in non-immunocompromised patients. The tumour cells morphologically resemble plasmablasts or immunoblasts and have abundant cytoplasmic IgM. related_terminology: Acceptable: HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS. Not recommended: large B-cell lymphoma arising in HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease (obsolete). essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: presentation with primary nodal and/or splenic involvement; effacement of architecture by large blasts / transformed B cells with generally plasmablastic, immunoblastic, or anaplastic morphology; positive immunostaining for LANA (KSHV/HHV8) and IgM. Desirable: absence of immunoglobulin somatic hypermutations; EBER in situ hybridization (usually negative but can be positive in some cases).

cards.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS definition: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS (PTCL-NOS) is a heterogeneous category of mature T-cell lymphomas that do not correspond to any of the specifically defined entities of mature T-cell lymphomas. related_terminology: Not recommended: T-cell lymphoma NOS; peripheral T-cell lymphoma, pleomorphic small cell; peripheral T-cell lymphoma, pleomorphic medium and large cell; peripheral T-cell lymphoma, large cell; Lennert lymphoma. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a mass-forming clonal T-cell proliferation with a variable histological appearance; exclusion of immunodeficiency-associated lymphoproliferative disorders other than lymphoma; exclusion of specific T-cell lymphomas (i.e. lymphoblastic lymphoma, anaplastic large cell lymphoma, EBV-associated lymphoma/lymphoproliferation, and cutaneous T-cell lymphomas). Desirable: involvement of more than one site; aberrant T-cell phenotype confirming neoplastic nature.

cards.title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS definition: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS) is a heterogeneous category of nodal and extranodal mature T-cell lymphomas that cannot be assigned to a specific PTCL entity, consisting of a broad cytomorphological spectrum of medium to large lymphoid cells with variable degrees of pleomorphism.

cards.title: Splenic B-cell lymphoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Splenic B-cell lymphoma definition: Primary splenic B-cell lymphomas (PSLs) are subtypes of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and include the primary splenic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which in the fifth edition of the WHO classification of haematolymphoid tumours has been renamed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS), and four small B-cell lymphomas: hairy cell leukaemia (HCL), splenic marginal zone lymphoma (SMZL), splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma (SDRPL), and splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukaemia with prominent nucleoli (SBLPN).

cards.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS
cards.excerpt: Entity: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS definition: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS (DLBCL-NOS) is a neoplasm of mature blastic B cells with a diffuse growth pattern. DLBCL-NOS encompasses all cases that do not belong to a specific diagnostic category of large B-cell lymphomas. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: architectural effacement by a diffuse proliferation of medium or large lymphoid cells with centroblastic or immunoblastic morphology; mature B-cell immunophenotype, TdT-negative; high Ki-67 index (but < 95%). Desirable: absence of MYC rearrangements; genetic testing, if relevant.

cards.title: High grade B cell lymphoma, NOS — May be applicable to de novo or transformed cases
cards.excerpt:
Note:
This diagnosis is rare and should be rendered only when diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and Burkitt lymphoma (BL) have been ruled out
Cases with large cell morphology that have MYC rearrangement with or without amplification / gain of BCL2 should be considered DLBCL
Pediatric cases with simple karyotypes and features of both DLBCL and BL have better prognosis than high grade B cell lymphoma, NOS and should instead be classified as either DLBCL or BL
Half of these cases harbor MYC rearrangements and can demonstrate a gene expression profile resembling that observed in BL (Blood 2008;112:1374)
Care should be taken before diagnosing a transformed follicular lymphoma as high grade B cell lymphoma, especially if any retained follicular architecture exists

Few studies have been conducted but this lymphoma may arise from germinal center B cells in 20 - 35% of cases with MYC rearrangement and amplification / gain of BCL2 (Mod Pathol 2015;28:208)
Cell of origin is unknown in cases without MYC or BCL2 rearrangements (Mod Pathol 2009;22:1507)

cards.title: High grade B cell lymphoma, NOS — Survival is typically measured in months
cards.excerpt:
This category may have a slightly better outcome than high grade B cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and / or BCL6 rearrangements (Am J Surg Pathol 2014;38:49, Br J Haematol 2013;162:40)
The worst prognosis has been reported in instances of amplification / gain of MYC with or without rearrangement of BCL2 or in instances of amplification / gain of BCL2 with or without rearrangement of MYC (Mod Pathol 2015;28:208, Cancer 2012;118:1566)
Poor outcome has been associated with age > 60 years, stage IV disease or a high International Prognostic Index (IPI) score (Br J Haematol 2013;162:40)

cards.title: High grade B cell lymphoma, NOS — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
No standardized treatment exists
This category is thought to be resistant to typical DLBCL, NOS and BL regimens, including rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone (R-CHOP)
Use of dose adjusted etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin with rituximab (DA-EPOCH-R) has been favored in some settings (Hsi: Hematopathology - Foundations in Diagnostic Pathology, 3rd Edition, 2017)

cards.title: DLBCL, NOS — Prognostic factors
cards.excerpt:
Unfavorable prognostic features:
Clinical: ↑ age, ↑ LDH, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) ≥ 2, Ann Arbor stage III / IV, extranodal disease, bulky disease (J Clin Oncol 2010;28:2373, Blood 2014;123:837)
Cell of origin status (Blood 2004;103:275):
Activated B cell subtype (~40%) and germinal center B cell subtype (~60%) associated with 5 year progression free survival rates of 40 - 50% versus 70 - 80%, respectively
MYC translocation (Blood 2015;126:2466)
Double expresser status: immunohistochemical coexpression of MYC (≥ 40% tumor cells) and BCL2 (≥ 50% tumor cells) in the absence of co-occurring MYC and BCL2 rearrangements

cards.title: Nodal T follicular helper cell lymphoma, NOS — Essential features
cards.excerpt:
Aggressive, mature T cell lymphoma
Expression of CD4 and at least 2, preferably 3, T follicular helper markers (such as PD-1, CD10, BCL6, CXCL13 and ICOS)
Part of a spectrum of T cell lymphomas with TFH phenotype, which also includes nodal TFH cell lymphoma, angioimmunoblastic type (nTFHL-AI), formerly angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma and nodal TFH cell lymphoma, follicular type (nTFHL-F), formerly known as follicular T cell lymphoma

cards.title: Nodal T follicular helper cell lymphoma, NOS — Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.excerpt:

2 recognized patterns: diffuse infiltration or proliferation around follicles in a paracortical T zone infiltration

cards.title: Neoplastic WBC — Smooth chromatin with inconspicuous nucleoli
cards.excerpt:
Moderate amount of pale blue cytoplasm classically seen with fine, hair-like projections
CD19+, CD20+ (bright), TRAP+, CD11c+, CD25+, CD103+, CD200+, annexin A1+ (most specific), CD5-, CD10- (80 - 90%), CD23-
Splenic B cell lymphoma / leukemia with prominent nucleoli (WHO 5th edition) and hairy cell leukemia variant (ICC 2022), a chronic lymphoproliferative disorder whose morphologic characters resemble hairy cell leukemia; neoplastic cells have prominent nucleoli and are negative for HCL markers (CD25, annexin A1 and TRAP)
BRAF V600E mutation is found in most (> 90%) classic hairy cell leukemia cases
